title: Space Rogue
build: Origin Systems' two-sided disk, G64 images of side 1 (SHA-256 f8f4bdd5…) and side 2 (944b0898…) from the C64 Preservation Project's collection (orientation.md)

records.c: The processor port: the title runs with $34 (all RAM, its pictures and shapes under the ROMs) and banks the I/O and the KERNAL in ($36) for the hardware, the loads and the interrupt
The block copiers' source pointer: draw_shape points it at a shape's colours, one screen-matrix row for every 8 pixel lines, and put_matrix_block copies from it
The block copiers' source, high byte
The shown buffer's screen matrix page, $60 or $E0 ($28A4)
The block copiers' width in bytes: draw_shape sets it to the shape's width before put_matrix_block

The block copiers' height in character rows. draw_shape sets it to the shape's height in lines divided by 8, rounded up ($2A2F), takes one off each time the lines it skips above the screen reach a new character row ($2A61), and clips it to the rows left below the shape's first ($2A8C). It counts from the shape's first line, so a shape that starts part-way down a character row covers one row more than it colours: the Sunracer's 56 lines from line 92 cover 8 rows and get 7
dissolve_in's source: the drawing buffer's page
The dissolves' destination: the shown buffer's page

The high seven bits of the dissolves' 15-bit shift register, Y holding the low eight: bits 0-4 pick a page of the 8 KB bitmap, bits 5-6 the pixel pair in the byte. It starts at $7FFF, shifts right with taps $60 into this byte, and stops when it comes back, so every nonzero value comes once
The drawing buffer's page, $40 or $C0: draw_shape and unpack_picture draw there, and show_drawn shows it
The cursor's character row, 0-24, for print_char, which nothing in the title calls
The cursor's column, 0-39, for print_char
The text window's left column, where print_char's new line starts
The text window's right column: a character that would go past it starts a new line first
The unpacker's and dissolve_in's source pointer; load_inline uses it to read its inline name and puts the caller's value back
The source pointer's high byte
The unpacker's and the dissolves' destination pointer
The destination pointer's high byte
Column × 8, the column's offset within a bitmap row (column_offset_of), low byte
The column's offset, high byte (0 or 1)
The shown buffer's page, $40 or $C0
The key the interrupt last saw, its low seven bits; $FF when none is waiting
Counted up by the interrupt once a frame; nothing in the title reads it

draw_shape's column, the X it was called with

The line's high byte: negative while the line is above the screen

The mask's pointer, high byte

draw_shape's copy of the width, the bytes it draws on each line
put_matrix_block's step through its source from row to row: draw_shape sets it to the shape's width
The shape's height in pixel lines
The lines draw_shape still has to draw, cut to what the screen shows
ANDed with every frequency the effect player writes; sound_init sets it to $FF

The second sound's enable mask, ANDed in before it plays: sound_init sets it to zero, the title sets it to $FF as the Sunracer's engine starts ($2BFE) and back to zero for the credits ($2D86) and on a key ($2F5C)
The second sound's target frequency, low byte: zero in the title ($2BA9)
The second sound's target frequency, high byte: zero at the start of each showing ($2BAB), then one more at each step of the lift-off, held at $FF, so the engine's note climbs
The second sound's frequency, low byte, stepped up by 2 a frame until it reaches the target; zeroed at the start of each showing ($2BA5)
The second sound's frequency, high byte
The second sound's sustain level, in the high nybble: $FF at the start of each showing ($2BAF), then two less at each step of the lift-off, down to zero, so the engine fades as it climbs
The effect's starting frequency, low byte (start_effect copies it from effect_freq_lo)
The effect's starting frequency, high byte
The effect's frequency step per frame, low byte
The effect's frequency step, high byte
The playing note's frequency, low byte
The playing note's frequency, high byte
The effect's attack and decay, for voice 1's $D405
The effect's sustain and release, for $D406
The effect's control byte for voice 1, waveform and gate ($81 noise, $41 pulse)
How many frames each repeat of the effect's note lasts
The frames-left count at which the note's gate is released
Frames left of the note playing; zero between notes
Repeats of the note still to start; $FF, negative, once the effect has finished
Not a variable: the operand of BIT $E8 at $22E8, a byte scan_keys branches into as an INX ($22EB)
The KERNAL's IRQ vector, pointed at irq_body ($226A) so the interrupt also works while the KERNAL is banked in for a load
The IRQ vector's high byte
The BRK vector, pointed at the RTI at $2264
The BRK vector's high byte
The KERNAL's NMI vector, pointed at the RTI at $2264, so RESTORE does nothing
The NMI vector's high byte

Not data: BIT $1EA5 at $2863 hides LDA $1E (show_drawn, $2864) in its operand

TITLE's first instruction, where BOOT's loader jumps: sets up the interrupt and the line table, loads SPACE, ROGUE, SHIP and CREDITS, clears the $4000 bitmap, turns the multicolour bitmap on with white colours and starts the lift-off (title_loop)
load_inline's argument: load to $B700, then the file name "SPACE" and a zero
Loads "ROGUE" to $AC00
load_inline's argument: load to $AC00, then the file name "ROGUE" and a zero
Loads "SHIP" to $6800
load_inline's argument: load to $6800, then the file name "SHIP" and a zero
Loads "CREDITS" to $3000
load_inline's argument: load to $3000, then the file name "CREDITS" and a zero
With the files in: clears the $4000 bitmap, sets the bitmap mode, shows the empty $4000 buffer with its colours, makes the colour RAM white and jumps to title_loop
Banks the I/O and the KERNAL in ($01 low bits %110, RAM at $A000), keeping A
Banks all RAM in ($01 low bits %100), keeping A

Loads the file named after the JSR: two bytes of load address (low, high), then the name ending in a zero, and returns past the zero. LOAD runs from device 8 with secondary address 0, so the file goes to that address whatever its header says, and is retried until the KERNAL reports no error; the caller's $30/$31 are kept in the patched loads at $20C3 and $20C7
The name's length, patched in by $208E
The name's address, low byte, patched in by $2096
The name's address, high byte, patched in by $209D
The load address's low byte, patched in by $2072
The load address's high byte, patched in by $2078
The caller's $30, patched in by $205A and put back on the way out
The caller's $31, patched in by $205F
Clears any key waiting, waits for the interrupt to put one in key ($3C), clears it again and returns it in A; nothing in the title calls it
Sets key ($3C) to $FF: none waiting

A wait of about 0.86 seconds that a key ends early (the key stays in $3C). clear_key leaves A at $FF, so the caller's A makes no difference: the 26-cycle loop always runs 255 + 254 + ... + 1 = 32,640 times (848,640 cycles), and the interrupt adds its share. The title's callers pass A = 0

Prints the character in A at the cursor, keeping A, the flags, and X and Y (put back by the patched loads at $2107 and $2109). The title never prints: it has no font loaded, and nothing calls this or the routines below it
The caller's X, patched in by $2101
The caller's Y, patched in by $20FE

Draws character A (bit 7 ignored) into the drawing buffer at the cursor: RETURN ($0D) starts a new line, $08 and $7F rub out the character before the cursor, and a character that would pass the window's right edge starts a new line first. Its 8 bytes would come from a font at $F200, which the title never loads
The cursor row's offset in a bitmap, low byte, patched in from char_row_offsets ($2156); the ADC adds the column's offset to it
The cursor row's offset, high byte, ORed with the drawing buffer's page ($215E)
The character's address in FONT, low byte, patched in by $2144
The character's address in FONT, high byte: built from character × 8 and then $F2 added ($214C)
The bitmap cell's address, low byte, patched in by $216B
The bitmap cell's address, high byte, patched in by $2172

Rubs out the character before the cursor: prints a space at the cursor, steps back two columns, prints another and steps back one, leaving the cursor a column to the left (the BPL at $218F lands on the next instruction either way)

Moves the cursor to the window's left column on the next row. Past row 24 it scrolls the drawing buffer's rows 1-24 up a character row instead (7,680 bytes) and clears only the first 64 bytes of the bottom row, 8 of its 40 cells: $21EF loads Y = 1 where the 320-byte row needs 2
new_line's scroll source, low byte, set to $40 (row 1 starts 320 bytes in)
new_line's scroll source page, the drawing buffer's plus one, stepped on each page
new_line's scroll destination page, the drawing buffer's own, stepped on each page
The bottom row's address, low byte, set to zero
The bottom row's page, the drawing buffer's plus $1E (row 24 starts 7,680 bytes in)
The byte counter new_line's two loops count down

With interrupts off, points every vector at the title's own handlers: a raster interrupt at line $50 with CIA1's interrupts off; the NMI and BRK vectors at the RTI at $2264 (it also writes that address to $FFFC, which a reset never reads from RAM); the KERNAL's IRQ vector ($0314) at irq_body and the hardware one ($FFFE) at irq. Then clears the key, sets up the SID (sound_init) and banks all RAM in. The title's first call ($2000)
An RTI: the NMI (RESTORE) and BRK do nothing
The raster interrupt as the hardware vector enters it, with all RAM banked in: pushes A, X and Y as the KERNAL's entry would and goes on into irq_body

The raster interrupt as $0314 enters it, the KERNAL having pushed the registers: saves $01, banks the I/O in, acknowledges the raster, scans the keyboard (a new or repeating key goes to key without bit 7), counts the frame in $3D, runs the effect player and returns

Scans the keyboard matrix itself; returns C set with a key's code in A when a key is new or repeating, C clear otherwise. CTRL and the two SHIFTs are read first and masked out of their rows; the first key held, row 7 down to row 0 and bit 7 down to bit 0 within a row, is numbered 8 × the row's place + the bit's and looked up in key_codes, or key_codes_shifted with either SHIFT, CTRL keeping only the low five bits. A held key repeats 36 frames after it went down, then every 6. Port A is left an input
BIT $E8 hides an INX ($E8) at $22E9: the first pass skips it and the BCS at $22EB lands on it, so X counts the row's released keys from bit 7 down to the one held
The last key's number, $FF for none
Frames left before a held key first repeats: 30 from a new key
Frames left before the next repeat: 6
For each row in scan order (7 down to 0), the bits of its modifier keys, ORed in so they never count as a key: CTRL in row 7, right SHIFT in row 6, left SHIFT in row 1
CTRL's bit from row 7, zero while it is held
Right SHIFT's bit from row 6, zero while it is held
Left SHIFT's bit from row 1, zero while it is held

The 64 keys' codes in scan order (row 7 bit 7 first): ASCII for letters (lower case), digits and punctuation, $0D for RETURN, $7F for DEL, $08 for the left-arrow key, $1B for F1, $09 and $0A for the cursor keys, and $80 for the keys with no code, which arrive as 0 since the interrupt keeps seven bits. The title only checks for any key
The same with a SHIFT held: capitals, the symbols over the digits, $0B for cursor up and $08 for cursor left
Silences the SID's three voices, turns the filter off and the volume up (15), and sets up the effect player and the masks

Starts sound effect A (0-4; others are ignored) on voice 1, copying its settings from the effect tables to $80-$8C with interrupts off; only play_effect calls it, and nothing in the title plays an effect

The effect player, run by the interrupt every frame: starts each repeat of the effect's note (frequency, envelope, waveform, gate), moves the frequency by the step each frame, releases the gate at the release point and silences the note when its frames run out. With no effect playing it plays a second sound: its frequency ($74/$75) slides up 2 a frame towards the target ($72/$73), and while drone_mask lets it through, voice 1 sounds it as noise at the level in $76, gated on and off on alternate frames. The title starts no effect; this second sound is the Sunracer's engine, which climbs and fades as the ship lifts off
Each effect's starting frequency, low byte, for effects 0-4
Effect 4's starting frequency, low byte, set by tone ($2618)
Each effect's starting frequency, high byte: $10, $18, $01, $80, and effect 4's
Effect 4's starting frequency, high byte, set by tone ($261B)
Each effect's frequency step per frame, low byte
Each effect's step, high byte: effect 0 falls by $80 a frame, effect 1 rises by $80, effect 2 falls by 2, effect 3 rises by $600, effect 4 holds
Each effect's attack and decay
Each effect's sustain and release
Each effect's waveform with the gate: noise ($81) for effects 0, 2 and 3, pulse ($41) for 1 and 4
Each effect's note length in frames: 32, 48, 128, 32, and effect 4's
Effect 4's note length, set by tone and silence ($2615)
The frames-left count at which each effect releases its gate
How many notes each effect plays: three for effect 1, one for the rest
Plays effect 3, rising noise, and waits for it: the intro's airlock sound, which the title carries in its copy of the library and never calls
Plays effect 1, three rising tones: the intro's alert, never called here
Plays effect 0, two 18-frame silences and effect 0 again: the intro's explosion, never called here
Plays effect 0, falling noise; only explosion_sound calls it
Plays effect 2, noise falling slowly for 128 frames: the intro's rumble, never called here
Plays effect A and waits until it has finished or a key is pressed; if a key is already waiting it plays nothing

Sends morse_text with tones (the elements' routines in morse_routines) until its closing zero or a key, which is then cleared: the intro's distress beacon. Nothing in the title calls it, so its patched operands still hold the file's $FF00
The Morse character's address, low byte, patched in and stepped
The Morse character's address, high byte
The element routine's address, low byte, patched into this JSR from morse_routines
The element routine's address, high byte

The distress call, SOS SOS PLAY ULTIMA SOS SOS: $AE a dot and $AD a dash, $A7 a short gap between the letters of SOS, $A0 a gap between the other letters and $AF a gap between words (the five codes are morse_symbols)
The five Morse characters distress_call looks up, in morse_routines' order: dot, dash, gap, word gap, short gap
The Morse elements' routines, a word each: morse_dot, morse_dash, morse_gap, silence_18 and silence_4
morse_routines read from one byte on, for the high bytes (Y = 2 × the element)
A dot: a 2-frame tone and 2 frames of silence
A dash: a 6-frame tone and 2 frames of silence
The gap between letters: 6 frames of silence
18 frames of silence (effect 4 at frequency 0): the gap between Morse words and the pause in explosion_sound
4 frames of silence, the gap between the letters of SOS
A tone at frequency $3864 lasting A frames
A frames of silence: effect 4 at frequency 0
Copies the colours to the colour RAM, then runs copy_matrix; nothing calls it

Copies 8 pages, a buffer's $2000-$27FF (screen matrix and colours), from page A ORed with $12 to the same place in the other buffer. Only dissolve_in calls it, with A = $1E, which makes the source $E000 whichever buffer is shown
copy_matrix's source page, patched in and stepped
copy_matrix's destination page, the source's with bit 7 flipped
Copies the $4000 buffer's picture to the $C000 buffer and the colours to the colour RAM; nothing calls it
Copies the $C000 buffer's picture to the $4000 buffer and the colours to the colour RAM; nothing calls it
Copies the shown buffer's picture to the drawing buffer (copy_shown) and its colours to the colour RAM; nothing in the title calls it
Copies the $4000 buffer's picture, bitmap, screen matrix and colours ($28 pages), to the $C000 buffer; only copy_4000_colours, which nothing calls, runs it
Copies the $C000 buffer's picture to the $4000 buffer; only copy_c000_colours runs it
Copies the shown buffer's picture to the drawing buffer; never run in the title, so its patched operands still hold $FF00
The picture copy's source page, patched in and stepped
The snapshot shows this STA's page left at $68, after a copy to the $4000 buffer
The picture copy's destination page, patched in and stepped
Sets $34/$35 to column A × 8

Returns character row A's offset in the drawing buffer, low byte in A and high in Y (with the buffer's page ORed in), X = 0; the caller's X is put back in the LDX at $26A1. Nothing in the title calls it
row_address's caller's X, patched in by $2693
Fills the colour RAM, $D800-$DBFF, with 1 (white), interrupts off: called once at the start ($203C), so every picture's third colour is white, whatever colours its file carries
The page of white_colours' STA, stepped from $D8; the snapshot shows it left at $DC
Copies a block, $14 bytes wide and $15 rows high, from ($10) into the colour RAM at column X of row Y (colour_rows), the source advancing by the width each row; nothing in the title calls it
put_colour_block's destination, low byte, patched in and stepped by 40
put_colour_block's destination, high byte

Copies a block, $14 bytes wide and $15 rows high, from ($10) into the drawing buffer's screen matrix at column X of row Y (matrix_rows), the source advancing by block_stride ($66) each row; entered at $270E for the $C000 buffer and $2712 for the $4000 one. draw_shape uses it to stamp a shape's colours
put_matrix_block's destination, low byte, patched in and stepped by 40
put_matrix_block's destination, high byte
Builds the pixel-line table at $EB00 (low bytes) and $EC00 (high): for each of the 200 lines, (line / 8) × 320 + line mod 8. The title's second call ($2003); draw_shape reads it
The offset build_line_table is working on, low byte; it leaves $1F40 (8,000) in the pair
The offset build_line_table is working on, high byte
Each character row's offset in a bitmap, 320 × the row, a word each for rows 0-24 (print_char, row_address: neither runs in the title)
char_row_offsets read from one byte on, for the high bytes (X = 2 × the row)
Each row's address in the colour RAM, $D800 + 40 × the row, a word each (put_colour_block, never called here)
colour_rows read from one byte on, for the high bytes
Each row's offset from a buffer's page to its screen matrix, $2000 + 40 × the row, a word each (put_matrix_block)
matrix_rows read from one byte on, for the high bytes

Turns the multicolour bitmap on ($D011 bit 5, $D016 bit 4), with the bitmap at the start of the VIC's bank and the screen matrix $2000 into it ($D018 = $80), and the background black. Its read-modify-write of $D011 also writes back bit 7, which reads as bit 8 of the beam's line and writes bit 8 of the raster compare: run while the beam is on line 256 or later, it moves the interrupt from line $50 to $150 (336), which no frame reaches, and the interrupt stops for good
Shows the $C000 buffer and copies its colours to the colour RAM; nothing calls it
Shows the $4000 buffer and copies its colours to the colour RAM: called once at the start ($2039), just before white_colours makes them all white
Shows the drawing buffer (show_drawn) and copies its colours to the colour RAM; nothing in the title calls it

Shows the $C000 buffer (the VIC's bank 3, CIA2 port A bits 0-1 = 0) and makes $4000 the drawing buffer. The BITs that follow hide two more entries in their operands, show_4000 (LDA #$40) and show_drawn (LDA $1E). Sets $3A to the shown buffer's page, $12 to its screen matrix's and $1E to the other buffer's
BIT $40A9: its operand is LDA #$40, show_4000's entry
Shows the $4000 buffer (the VIC's bank 1, CIA2 port A bits 0-1 = %10) and makes $C000 the drawing buffer; the LDA #$40 here is the operand of the BIT at $2860
BIT $1EA5: its operand is LDA $1E, show_drawn's entry
Shows the drawing buffer, the shown one becoming the drawing buffer: the flip after each frame of the animation is drawn; the LDA $1E here is the operand of the BIT at $2863
Clears the drawing buffer's bitmap, 32 pages; the BITs that follow hide entries for the $4000 buffer ($28B4) and the $C000 one ($28B7). Only clear_4000 is called
BIT $40A9: its operand is LDA #$40, clear_4000's entry
Clears the $4000 buffer's bitmap ($4000-$5FFF), called once at the start ($2033); the LDA #$40 here is the operand of the BIT at $28B3
BIT $C0A9: its operand is LDA #$C0, an entry at $28B7 for the $C000 buffer
The page clear_drawing's STA writes, patched in and stepped; the snapshot shows it left at $60

Brings the drawing buffer's picture onto the shown one a pixel pair at a time in a scattered order, after copying its colours to the colour RAM and its screen matrix to the shown buffer (copy_matrix); a 15-bit shift register visits every pixel pair of the 8 KB bitmap once (dissolve_lfsr). The title enters 3 bytes in, at dissolve_in_matrix ($28D1), so the colour RAM stays white
dissolve_in without its first step, the colours: the title's dissolves come in here, so the colour RAM stays white
The pixel pair from the drawing buffer, patched into this ORA by $290B
The four pixel pairs of a multicolour byte, left to right
The bits each pixel pair leaves alone, the complements of pixel_masks
Fades the shown picture to black a pixel pair at a time, in the shift register's scattered order: the credits fade out this way ($2DA7)
The complements of pixel_masks again, for dissolve_out

Unpacks the picture packed at page A into the drawing buffer: a byte below $80 is a count and the next byte is repeated that many times; $80 plus a count is followed by that many bytes to copy; a zero is followed by the border colour, which is stored too, written to $D020, and ends it. A whole picture is a buffer's bitmap, its screen matrix at +$2000 and its colours at +$2400

Copies the shown buffer's colours (its +$2400) to the colour RAM: first to $0C00 with all RAM banked in, then on to $D800 with the I/O in, since the RAM under the KERNAL and the colour RAM cannot both be seen at once. In the title it runs once, from show_4000_colours at the start
colours_to_ram's source page, the shown buffer's plus $24, stepped
colours_to_ram's staging page, from $0C, stepped
The staging page read back, from $0C, stepped
The colour RAM page written, from $D8, stepped

Draws a shape from SHIP into the drawing buffer at column X and pixel line A × 256 + Y (A negative while the shape is above the screen). The shape is $64 bytes a line, one byte per cell across, $67 lines high, from ($60). With $4E bit 7 set it is drawn through its mask at ($62): each screen byte keeps only the pixels the mask leaves clear and takes the shape's; otherwise its bytes are stored over the screen. With bit 6 set its colours are stamped first, a screen-matrix row from ($10) for every 8 lines (put_matrix_block). Lines above the top are skipped and lines past line 199 cut off
Skips the lines above the screen one at a time, stepping the shape, the mask and, every eighth line, the colours, until the line is on the screen or the shape has run out
Clips the height to the lines left above line 200 and the colour rows to the 25 the screen has
Bit 6 of $4E: stamps the shape's colours over its rows of the screen matrix
Bit 7 of $4E: draws through the mask (masked_lines); otherwise stores the bytes (plain_lines)

Stores each visible line of the shape over the screen: the line's address from the line table plus the column's offset, ORed with the drawing buffer's page, patched into the STA, which steps 8 bytes, a cell, for each byte
The screen byte plain_lines writes, low byte, patched in from the line table and stepped a cell at a time
The screen byte's high byte; the snapshot shows the STA left at $5F07, in the $4000 buffer
Draws each visible line through the mask: the screen byte ANDed with the mask byte inverted, then ORed with the shape's byte
The screen byte masked_lines reads, low byte, patched in with the STA's
The screen byte masked_lines reads, high byte; the snapshot shows it left at $D3C6, in the $C000 buffer
The screen byte masked_lines writes back, the same address as the AND's, low byte
The screen byte masked_lines writes back, high byte
The title's main loop: clears the key, then shows the lift-off over and over until a key is pressed, when it goes to title_exit

One showing: puts the scenery, the legs, the ship and the dust back at their starting lines, the dust at its first frame and the engine's note at zero and full level, draws the first frame and dissolves it in; then the stages, each followed by a check for a key: the engine starting, the rise, the legs folding, the climb and the credits
A key: go to title_exit
Z clear when a key is waiting ($3C is not $FF)
Six frames of the Sunracer standing on the plain; then the engine starts (drone_mask $FF) and twelve frames of dust blow out under it, the engine's note rising a step a frame
24 frames: the ship and its legs rise a pixel line a frame, the engine's note rising and its level falling
12 frames: the ship rises two lines a frame and the legs four, folding up into it

The ship climbs off the top of the screen while the planet falls away: from here the frames are drawn over ROGUE, the Space Rogue logo, without the legs. 12 frames with the ship up 2 lines and the scenery down 1, then 12 with the scenery down 2
Then 48 frames with the ship up 2 lines and the scenery down 3: the scenery is past the bottom of the screen and the ship past the top before they end
Silences the engine, unpacks CREDITS and dissolves it in, leaves it up for 24 pauses of about 0.86 seconds (about 21 seconds), fades it out and waits 6 more pauses on the black screen
The first frame, drawn over SPACE: the scenery, the legs and the ship, dissolved in rather than flipped
A frame of the ship standing, over SPACE: the scenery, the legs and the ship, then the flip
A frame of the lift-off over SPACE: the scenery, the legs, the small dust at its next frame, the ship and the large dust, then the flip
A frame of the climb over ROGUE: the scenery, the small dust, the ship and the large dust, then the flip
Draws the mountains (40 cells by 48 lines through their mask, with colours) at the line in $42/$43 and the plain under them (40 by 80, stored over the screen, with colours) at the line in $40/$41
Draws the landing legs, 23 cells by 24 lines through their mask, at column 9 and the line in $46/$47
Steps the dust's frame counter (0-7) and draws the small dust cloud's frame for it, 10 cells by 32 lines with itself as the mask, at column 15 and the line in $44/$45
The small dust's frame for each count 0-7, as an offset into dust_frames_small: frames 0, 1, 2, 0, 2, 1, 0, 2
The small dust's three frames in SHIP, a word each: $8600, $8740, $8880
dust_frames_small read from one byte on, for the high bytes
A colour address for each small dust frame, the next frame's start: draw_dust_small sets it but leaves bit 6 of $4E clear, so it is never used
